name: numbeo_api_cost_of_living
what_it_holds: Scrapy-based scraper + Flask REST API + SQLite store for 12 cost-of-living indicators per city (meals, transport, utilities, internet, rent) scraped from Numbeo's public pages; JWT auth layer. No committed dataset, MIT license, 28 commits, marked 'under development'.
why_useful: Most-starred/likely most-maintained unofficial Numbeo client if the team ever gets ToS clearance to build a recurring cost-of-living/affordability panel.
themes: Currency and travel affordability crowdsourced data: Numbeo, Expatistan, hotel price indices (Hotels.com HPI archives), Trivago Hotel Price Index, Kayak price trackers
why_all: Most-starred/likely most-maintained unofficial Numbeo client if the team ever gets ToS clearance to build a recurring cost-of-living/affordability panel.
Another reusable Numbeo scraper with a persistence layer already built (SQLite), which is closer to a repeatable point-in-time capture pipeline than a one-shot script.

name: expatistan
what_it_holds: Ruby API client for Expatistan's cost-of-living comparison data (Numbeo's main crowdsourced competitor). No committed dataset. MIT license, low activity (last updated 2019).
why_useful: Only Expatistan-specific repo found; gives a second crowdsourced cost-of-living source (city-pair comparisons) distinct from Numbeo, useful for cross-checking any affordability index built from Numbeo alone.
themes: Currency and travel affordability crowdsourced data: Numbeo, Expatistan, hotel price indices (Hotels.com HPI archives), Trivago Hotel Price Index, Kayak price trackers
why_all: Only Expatistan-specific repo found; gives a second crowdsourced cost-of-living source (city-pair comparisons) distinct from Numbeo, useful for cross-checking any affordability index built from Numbeo alone.

name: data-analysis-tools-bureau-of-justice-statistics
what_it_holds: An independent third-party profile/catalog of the Bureau of Justice Statistics (BJS) public API surface and its data-analysis tools, maintained by 'API Evangelist' as part of a broader series cataloguing US government APIs. Updated 2026-09-12 (very recent). Points to the BJS API itself rather than committing data.
why_useful: BJS runs the National Crime Victimization Survey and other crime/safety series with different (survey-based, victimization-rate) methodology than FBI UCR/NIBRS -- a useful complement if crime-as-demand-shock work needs a victimization-rate cross-check by region.
time_coverage: points to BJS's own historical API coverage, not itself a dataset
themes: Insurance, safety and travel advisories datasets (State Dept advisories history, travel insurance claims, crime by city) as demand shocks
why_all: BJS runs the National Crime Victimization Survey and other crime/safety series with different (survey-based, victimization-rate) methodology than FBI UCR/NIBRS -- a useful complement if crime-as-demand-shock work needs a victimization-rate cross-check by region.

name: hackforla/311-data
what_it_holds: Hack for LA civic-tech project ingesting the full MyLA311 service-request feed (all LA complaint types, includes the STR/short-term-rental enforcement category as one of many) via the LA Socrata API; project states CSV and parquet snapshots are also mirrored at huggingface.co (external host, exact dataset name/size not confirmed by page content). No Airbnb-specific filtering or documentation in the repo itself.
why_useful: LA is one of the three target cities (MyLA311). This is the most substantial, actively-maintained pipeline/mirror for LA's full 311 feed found; a team member would still need to filter to the STR/illegal-rental complaint category themselves to build the enforcement-activity proxy for gap area (311/STR enforcement) — not itself an Airbnb-labeled dataset.
themes: Short-term-rental insurance/incident, noise complaint and 311 datasets mentioning Airbnb (NYC 311, LA MyLA311, SF 311) as enforcement/activity proxies
why_all: LA is one of the three target cities (MyLA311). This is the most substantial, actively-maintained pipeline/mirror for LA's full 311 feed found; a team member would still need to filter to the STR/illegal-rental complaint category themselves to build the enforcement-activity proxy for gap area (311/STR enforcement) — not itself an Airbnb-labeled dataset.

name: ishitakapoor7/311derful
what_it_holds: Generic NYC 311 ETL tool pulling Socrata dataset erm2-nwe9 ('311 Service Requests from 2020 to Present', 22,145,244 rows, Jan 2020-Aug 2026) plus community-district boundaries (5crt-au7u); caches monthly gzipped CSVs into DuckDB. No Airbnb/STR filtering built in, but the underlying feed includes NYC's 'Illegal Home Sharing/Vacation Rental' complaint type handled by the Office of Special Enforcement, so this is a ready one-command pull method that could be filtered post-hoc.
why_useful: Point-in-time-capable, current (through Aug 2026), full-complaint-type NYC 311 pull method; fills the acquisition-method half of gap area on 311 enforcement proxies for NYC even though the repo itself does no STR-specific work.
last_activity: recent (data through Aug 2026 implies active maintenance)
duplicate_of_holding: Partially overlaps NYC OSE registry already held (item 34, municipal STR registries) but this is the raw 311 complaint stream, a different data type
themes: Short-term-rental insurance/incident, noise complaint and 311 datasets mentioning Airbnb (NYC 311, LA MyLA311, SF 311) as enforcement/activity proxies
why_all: Point-in-time-capable, current (through Aug 2026), full-complaint-type NYC 311 pull method; fills the acquisition-method half of gap area on 311 enforcement proxies for NYC even though the repo itself does no STR-specific work.
